extracted.intended_audience: Design proprietors, patent/design agents, and legal practitioners handling design registration and enforcement in the United Kingdom
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and statutory requirements for registration, protection, marking, inspection, assignment, and enforcement of registered designs under the Designs Act/Rules (UK). Covers application forms, drawings/specimens, classes of goods, term and cessation of copyright, exhibition exceptions, and remedies for infringement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility to apply
rubrics_metrics.description: The comptroller may, on application by or on behalf of any person claiming to be the proprietor of any new or original design not previously published in the United Kingdom, register the design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design must be 'new or original' and not previously published in the UK. 'Proprietor' is defined (see separate criterion). Useful vs ornamental distinction abolished — any novel design in the proper sense is acceptable; useful designs involving mechanical action may be patent subject-matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application form and manner
rubrics_metrics.description: Application must be made in the form set forth in the First Schedule or such other prescribed form (Form E), left at or sent by post to the Patent Office (Designs Branch) in the prescribed manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form E (Designs Forms) is the prescribed form; documents may be sent by post; agent may sign. Receipt will be acknowledged; if accepted a certificate of registration is forwarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of application
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must contain a statement of the nature of the design, and the class or classes of goods in which the applicant desires registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State name and address of proprietor, class(es) (see classes of goods), whether applicable for pattern/shape, and means by which it is applicable. Must bear proper stamp/fee and be signed by applicant or authorised agent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classes of goods and classification rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles are divided into specified classes (e.g., metal articles; jewellery; wood/bone; glass/earthenware; paper; leather; hangings; carpets; lace; millinery/apparel; textile fabrics; goods not included elsewhere; printed/woven textile designs; handkerchiefs/shawls).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same design may be registered in more than one class. If doubt exists as to proper class, comptroller may decide. See Designs Rules 16–20 for classification details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty and originality requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A design entitled to registration must (1) be new or original, and (2) must not have been previously published in the United Kingdom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case law examples: portraits copied from photographs not 'new and original'; a new combination of old designs may be new/original if constituting one design. Publication in UK destroys eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings/photographs/specimens required
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant shall furnish the prescribed number of copies of drawings, photographs, or tracings sufficient to enable identification, or may furnish exact representations or specimens of the design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usually three copies in addition to original (Designs Rules). Drawings/photographs/tracings/specimens must be fixed and on strong wide-ruled foolscap paper (13 by 8 inches) with specified margins; size and submission rules set in Designs Rules 8–9. Comptroller may refuse unsuitable representations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comptroller's discretion and refusal procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The comptroller may, if he thinks fit, refuse to register any design presented for registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before refusing an application, the comptroller gives ten days' notice to the applicant; applicant may notify desire to be heard within five days. Refusal may be appealed to the Board of Trade (see appeal procedure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal to Board of Trade (registration refusal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person aggrieved by the comptroller's refusal may appeal to the Board of Trade which may hear the applicant and comptroller and make an order determining whether and subject to what conditions registration is to be permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice of appeal must be left at the Patent Office within one month in Form F with required stamp and an unstamped copy, accompanied by statement of grounds. Board will appoint hearing day with seven days' notice unless shorter directed. See Designs Rules 16–20.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees and stamping requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees for applications, registration and other matters under this part are to be prescribed with Treasury sanction and levied to Her Majesty's Exchequer in prescribed manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: stamp for one design single articles (except classes 13,14) 10s; classes 13,14 1s; set of articles 1£. Fees for various procedures appear in Designs Rules and First Schedule. Failure to pay prescribed fees may affect rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term of copyright in registered designs
rubrics_metrics.description: When a design is registered the proprietor shall have copyright in the design during five years from the date of registration, subject to the provisions of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section fixes five years for all designs (abolishes varying terms under previous Acts). 'Subject to provisions' refers to furnishing specimens before sale, marking requirements, and events causing cessation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Furnishing exact representations/specimens before sale
rubrics_metrics.description: Before delivery on sale of any articles to which a registered design has been applied, the proprietor must, if exact representations or specimens were not furnished on the application, furnish to the comptroller the prescribed number of exact representations or specimens; failure allows comptroller to erase the name from the register and copyright shall cease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If drawings/tracings were furnished initially, three specimens must be furnished before sale; otherwise copyright is lost. See Designs Rules 9 and section 48.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking requirement before sale
rubrics_metrics.description: Before delivery on sale of any articles to which a registered design has been applied, the proprietor shall cause each such article to be marked with the prescribed mark, or with prescribed word(s) or figures denoting that the design is registered; failure results in cessation of copyright unless proprietor shows he took all proper steps to ensure marking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two prescribed marks: articles in classes 13 and 14 (printed or woven textile piece goods, handkerchiefs, shawls) to be marked 'REG'; articles in other classes to be marked 'RE' and the number on certificate of registration. Designs Rules 82 set particulars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspection of registered designs (during copyright)
rubrics_metrics.description: During existence of copyright the design shall not be open to inspection except by the proprietor, person authorised in writing by proprietor, person authorised by comptroller, or by Court, and then only in presence of comptroller (or officer) and on payment of the prescribed fee; no copy may be taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspector must furnish information enabling identification. Fee arrangements set by Designs Rules (per quarter hour etc.). This protects proprietors' rights while copyright subsists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspection when copyright has ceased
rubrics_metrics.description: When copyright in a design has ceased, the design shall be open to inspection and copies may be taken by any person on payment of the prescribed fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anyone may inspect the register or obtain copies on payment (e.g., 1s per quarter hour or fee by agreement); Designs Rules 33 govern fees and copying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information as to existence of copyright
rubrics_metrics.description: On request by any person producing a design or its mark of registration or furnishing information enabling identification, and on payment of the prescribed fee, the comptroller must inform whether registration still exists and in respect of what class(es), date of registration, and name/address of registered proprietor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application made in Form N; fee example given as 5s. Designs Rules 35 permit searches and comparative identification of identical or obvious imitation for designs registered since commencement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cesser of copyright for foreign but not domestic use
rubrics_metrics.description: If a registered design is used in manufacture in any foreign country and is not used in the United Kingdom within six months of its registration in this country, the copyright in the design shall cease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to prevent overseas-only registrations that bar UK manufacture. 'Country' means United Kingdom. Substantial (not nominal) user in UK is required; nominal user may be considered evasion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register of Designs content and evidentiary effect
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall be kept a Register of Designs recording names/addresses of proprietors, notifications of assignments and transmissions, and other prescribed matters; the register is prima facie evidence of matters directed to be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certified and sealed extracts from the register are receivable in evidence. Register continues previous registers; entries should be updated promptly (Form M for corrections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration of assignments/transmissions and particulars of title
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignments, transmissions, licences, and changes of proprietor should be registered by application in prescribed form (Form K) with particulars of title (e.g., probate, letters of administration, trustee certificate, assignment/licence documents) and accompanied by declaration verifying statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee equals registration fee for a design in the relevant class. Agent may sign if authorised; Designs Rules 22–25 set procedure; Orders of Court rectifying register are entered (Designs Rules 28).

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial/international exhibition exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Exhibiting a design or article at a Board of Trade‑certified industrial or international exhibition, or publishing a description during the holding, shall not prevent registration or invalidate it provided (a) exhibitor gives prescribed notice to comptroller before exhibiting/publishing, and (b) application for registration is made before or within six months from opening of the exhibition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain Board of Trade certificate that exhibition is industrial/international; give notice in Form L seven days before exhibition/publishing (Form L fee 6s), include brief description and sketch/drawing. See Designs Rules 36.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of infringement/piracy
rubrics_metrics.description: It is unlawful for any person without licence or written consent of registered proprietor to apply the design, or any fraudulent or obvious imitation thereof, in the class(es) of goods for which the design is registered for purposes of sale; also unlawful to publish or expose for sale any article to which such design has been applied, knowing the application was without consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Purpose of sale' means sale at any time (not limited to copyright term). Application where sale is not intended or application to other classes than registered may not be infringement. Ignorance of registration is not a defence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties and remedies for infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: Person infringing this section shall be liable for each offence to forfeit a sum not exceeding £50 to the proprietor, recoverable as simple contract debt; registered proprietor may instead bring an action for damages for losses arising from application or sale of pirated design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proprietor may elect penalty or damages. Actions may be brought in County Court or High Court (cost rules apply — e.g., limited costs in High Court for small sums). No statutory provision for delivery up of unsold pirated articles in this Act (but case law may provide remedies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of registered right (classes limitation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The exclusive right conferred by registration ('copyright') is to apply the design to articles in the class or classes in which the design is registered; application to other classes is not covered by the right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Infringement requires application in the registered class(es). Register entry and classes determine territorial/field scope of protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Design' (substantive scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Design' means any design applicable to any article of manufacture or to any substance (artificial/natural/partly so), whether applicable for pattern, shape/configuration, ornament, or any two or more purposes, by whatever means (printing, painting, embroidering, weaving, modelling, casting, embossing, engraving, staining, or other manual/mechanical/chemical means), excluding sculptures and matters protected by Sculpture Copyright Act 1814.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a broad functional/formal definition — both ornament and shape are included; distinction between useful and ornamental abolished for registration purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Copyright' in registered designs
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Copyright' means the exclusive right to apply a design to any article of manufacture or such substance in the class or classes in which the design is registered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the statutory exclusive field of protection; subject to provisions like furnishing specimens, marking, and cessation events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Proprietor' and persons entitled
rubrics_metrics.description: The author of any new and original design shall be considered the proprietor unless the work was executed for another for good/valuable consideration; persons acquiring a new and original design or the right to apply it for value, or persons on whom property devolves, are proprietors to the extent of their acquired rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Four classes: (a) the author; (b) the person who executed the design for a good/valuable consideration; (c) the person acquiring the design or right to apply it; (d) the person on whom the property devolves. Case law (e.g., Lazarus v. Charles) interpreted rights under earlier Acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice on application formality and documentary standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications, drawings, sketches, photographs, or tracings must follow prescribed physical and documentary formats (paper size, margins, fixation, number of copies); applications must bear proper stamp and may be signed by agent; documents may be posted; receipts acknowledged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper size 13x8 inches, left margin at least 1.5 inches; three exactly similar drawings/photographs/tracings or three specimens if articles can be pasted into books. Originals and copies requirements discussed in Designs Rules 8–9 and Practice notes.
